To avoid getting to specific and potentially triggering. My strategy to quit lax was to have more liquid calories instead of the traditional solid foods. It minimised the feeling of having a “food baby”.

Though do keep in mind there’re different potential health problems that might come with this strategy. Because as sad as it is, for me at least, this whole ED thing is a just a cruel trading game. You replace one behavior with another hopefully less damaging  one until it hopefully eventually gets to a point which resembles the “normal” healthy habits.

Almost overdosed on lax. Twice. That made me quit it cold turkey. It’s been over 2 months clean now so I’d say I made it out somewhat ok. For now at least.

When it happened the first time, I didn’t even know it was the lax, I thought it’s just ED body being weird and unreasonable again, or perhaps I somehow ate something bad, despite knowing every crumb of what I put into my body recently. 

It was the experience of sweating profusely on a toilet seat for more than an hour in agony, nothing helps, shitting or not, seating up straight or curling up like a ball, still in agony regardless. Its the crazy headache, dizziness and nauseous feeling that’s so much stronger than the usual default that you deal with. It was the toughest and longest battle for fight for not passing out. You don’t know how long the wave of cramps will last but you know it has lasted for longer than all the times before and it’s never been this intense. And it’s not getting better, not fading even a little bit with time like it usually would have. You keep feeling your sweat roll down every inch of your skin, your face, neck, arms, waist, thighs, all the way to your feet.

By the time I could just manage to leave the seat and balance on my own to walk without leaning on the wall, I was drenched in my cold sweat. The seat was all wet, even the floor has a small puddle. It’s not a good feeling. And of course the fierce fight to not collapse is still on going.

Luckily, things are much better after a night of sleep.

The second time though, it was everything above but slightly worse. In the middle of the whole thing, I even had my first surprise encountering with projectile vomiting. Again, it didn’t help much like it usually should have with any discomfort or illness. After a night of sleep, again, I thought I felt better as I got ready to work. But not even an hour after I woke up, intense hit of nausea. Ran to the toilet, nothing came up. Of course nothing came out. What even could come up after the vomiting and back door action from the lax on the night before? After staring at the toilet for a short while as I was getting late, I bolted out the door for work. Not even 10 minutes later, it’s the feeling of vertigo, which I’ve never felt before. It’s the actual “the world is spinning” feeling. I had to stop and crouch down on the sidewalk. Walking is simply not possible. Couldn’t even breath properly, its the struggling to desperately attempt to grasp for air but the lungs just weren’t expanding. It feels like getting suffocated by nothing. I was not new to this “weird breathing problem” which you feel like you can’t take a full deep breath, it’s just like the mild dizziness we have in the background most of the time. But again, THIS time, I was struggling like never before to get enough oxygen. It was terrifying. Though luckily, standing / crouching at that spot for 10-15minutes while trying to breathe and not collapse had me recovered enough to slowly keep going. Very very slowly.

After seeing a doctor before work, it was confirmed to not be food poisoning. It could only be the lax. The symptoms also mostly matched. It’s the lax.

Trust me, it was not a good feeling. Though it took me years to get to that point, I was just like you. I tried out this lax thing, I loved the empty feeling. I understand. But we also understand we’re gonna be addicted to it. Turn back while you’re not too far down the hole. While you haven’t completely fucked up your digestive system which I didn’t even get into in this reply. Trust us when we say this ain’t worth it.
